findings.evidence: upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:388 `def IsOrthogonal`, :398 `lemma isOrthogonal_of_forall_apply_same`; code .../OrthogonalProjection.lean:169 `lemma reflect_isometry ... : g.IsOrthogonal (reflect g u)`; code .../SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:25 `lemma isOrthogonal_id`.
findings.fix: Rename to `isOrthogonal_reflect` (or `reflect_isOrthogonal`), and rename the field to `isOrthogonal`, updating `hf.isometry` uses at DIS/Tensors/Basic.lean:510, 533, 551, 989.
findings.issue: `reflect_isometry` now concludes `g.IsOrthogonal (reflect g u)`, but the name still says "isometry" — the word of the `Bilin.IsIsometry` this PR deleted. In Mathlib `Isometry` is a different (metric-space) notion, and the PR's own sibling lemma spells the predicate out (`LinearMap.isOrthogonal_id`, SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:25), as does Mathlib's `LinearMap.isOrthogonal_of_forall_apply_same`. Same mismatch on the structure field `IsKinematicStabilizer.isometry : g.IsOrthogonal f` (DIS/Tensors/Basic.lean:448), whose type this PR changed.

findings.evidence: Jets/Frame/Basic.lean:292 `(hc : 0 < c)` vs lines 300/305/311 `(hc : c ≠ 0)`, all named `…_eq_of_n_eq_smul`; naming conventions, "hypotheses described with `of` to disambiguate".
findings.fix: Rename to `energy_eq_of_n_eq_smul_of_pos` (or `energy_eq_of_n_eq_smul_pos`), so the hypothesis distinguishing it from the `c ≠ 0` siblings appears in the name.
findings.issue: `energy_eq_of_n_eq_smul` requires `0 < c`, while the three sibling lemmas with the identical name shape (`spatialPart_eq_of_n_eq_smul`:300, `spatialNorm_eq_of_n_eq_smul`:305, `cosAngle_eq_of_n_eq_smul`:311) require only `c ≠ 0`. The name gives no hint that this one is the restricted case, although the same file marks positivity elsewhere (`cosAngle_smul_left_of_pos`:263).

summary: Names are mostly accurate and well placed (dot notation on LinearMap.BilinForm, no notation introduced), but `reflect_isometry` keeps terminology the PR itself deleted in favour of Mathlib's `IsOrthogonal`, and `energy_eq_of_n_eq_smul` hides a strictly stronger hypothesis than its three identically-shaped siblings.
